nodes.content: Enable speech–gesture reference resolution that distinguishes gesture-dependent meaning from speaker-specific correlations under uncertain cross-modal timing.
requirements: Achieve ≥10 percentage-point accuracy gains over speech-only models on gesture-dependent references from unseen speakers.
Limit accuracy degradation to 5 percentage points under irrelevant-gesture substitutions and ±300-millisecond audiovisual offsets.

nodes.content: Train ShiftGuard using speaker-adversarial embeddings, ±300 ms temporal marginalization, irrelevant-gesture invariance, and label-updated relevant-gesture swaps.
Can label-updated gesture swaps preserve referent-bearing motion while speaker-adversarial training removes identity cues under ±300 ms jitter?
ShiftGuard’s label-updated swaps and speaker-adversarial training yield ≥10-point accuracy gains over speech-only on unseen-speaker GestureRef, with ≤5-point ±300-ms jitter/irrelevant-swap loss.
Train ShiftGuard and swap/adversary ablations on speaker-disjoint GestureRef; measure speech-only gains, speaker-probe accuracy, and ±300-ms/irrelevant-gesture losses.
Evaluate ShiftGuard and swap/adversary ablations on speaker-disjoint GestureRef: referent accuracy versus speech-only, speaker-probe accuracy, and irrelevant-swap/±300-ms degradation.
On unseen-speaker GestureRef, referent accuracy was 76% versus speech-only 64%; irrelevant-swap/±300-ms-jitter losses were 3/4 points; binary speaker-probe accuracy was 52%.
Advance ShiftGuard to independent replication: its 12-point gain and 3/4-point robustness losses meet both thresholds.
Replicate ShiftGuard on independent GestureRef-2 speakers, measuring speech-only accuracy gains and worst-case irrelevant-gesture and ±300-ms offset losses.
GestureRef-2 replication report with independent speaker splits, ShiftGuard checkpoints, speech-only comparisons, and irrelevant-gesture/±300-ms offset accuracy tables.
Can temporal marginalization identify the correct referent when two nearby pointing gestures target different objects within ±300 ms?
On competing-point GestureRef-2 trials, ShiftGuard stays within 5 accuracy points of aligned trials at ±300 ms, outperforming nearest-gesture alignment.
Score ShiftGuard and nearest-gesture alignment on GestureRef-2 competing-point trials at 0 and ±300 ms; compare referent-accuracy drops.
On GestureRef-2 competing-point trials, ShiftGuard accuracy fell from 74% aligned to 62% at +300 ms; nearest-gesture scored 58%.
Add deictic-word-anchored gesture assignment to ShiftGuard, trained with competing-point negatives to prevent target blending under audiovisual offsets.
Train anchored ShiftGuard with competing-point negatives; evaluate speaker-disjoint GestureRef-2 against speech-only and baseline under irrelevant swaps and ±300-ms offsets.
Initialize anchored ShiftGuard from GestureRef-2 replication checkpoints; reuse its speaker splits to train competing-point negatives and test offset robustness.
Anchored ShiftGuard checkpoint and GestureRef-2 competing-point negative pairs, with fixed speaker splits and ±300-ms offset evaluation scripts.
Evaluate anchored and original ShiftGuard checkpoints using GestureRef-2 competing-point pairs: unseen-speaker accuracy, speech-only gains, irrelevant-swap and ±300-ms losses.
On GestureRef-2 competing-point trials, anchored scored 78%/75% aligned/+300 ms versus original 74%/62%; speech-only 64%; anchored irrelevant-swap loss: 3 points.
Does anchored ShiftGuard retain its accuracy gain on gesture-dependent references without explicit deictic words?
Anchored ShiftGuard’s 14-point competing-point advantage persists as ≥10-point speech-only gains on implicit-deixis trials, with ≤5-point ±300-ms loss.
Evaluate anchored ShiftGuard versus speech-only on speaker-disjoint GestureRef-2 implicit-deixis trials, reporting aligned accuracy and worst ±300-ms loss.
On unseen-speaker GestureRef-2 implicit-deixis trials, anchored scored 76% versus speech-only 65%; worst ±300-ms accuracy was 72%.
Advance anchored ShiftGuard to deployment validation: competing-point/implicit-deixis gains are 14/11 points, with ≤4-point offset and 3-point irrelevant-swap losses.
Validate anchored ShiftGuard on fresh speakers’ implicit-deixis clips, measuring speech-only gains and irrelevant-gesture/±300-ms losses.
Train a counterfactual gesture-relevance gate using irrelevant-swap negatives and offset-averaged alignment, falling back to speech-only when gesture evidence is weak.
Can the relevance gate reject irrelevant gestures without suppressing implicit-deixis cues under ±300-ms audiovisual offsets?
On unseen-speaker GestureRef-2, gating limits irrelevant-swap loss to ≤2 points while preserving ≥10-point implicit-deixis gain and ≤5-point offset loss.
Using GestureRef-2 replication splits and checkpoints, train the relevance gate; test implicit-deixis gains and irrelevant-swap/±300-ms losses on unseen speakers.
On unseen-speaker GestureRef-2 implicit-deixis, gating scored 72% versus speech-only 65%, a 7-point gain; irrelevant-swap/±300-ms losses were 1/3 points.
Replacing hard rejection with soft gesture–referent gating should recover ≥10-point implicit-deixis gains, retaining ≤2-point irrelevant-swap and ≤5-point offset losses.
Train soft gesture–referent gating on GestureRef-2; compare hard gating on unseen-speaker implicit-deixis gains and swap/offset losses.
Train soft gesture–referent gating and compare against hard gating on GestureRef-2 implicit-deixis gains, irrelevant-swap losses, and ±300-ms offsets.
On unseen-speaker GestureRef-2 implicit-deixis, soft gating scored 76% versus speech-only 65% and hard gating 72%; irrelevant-swap/±300-ms losses: 2/4 points.
Adopt soft gating over hard gating: it matches anchored ShiftGuard’s 76% implicit-deixis accuracy with 2/4-point substitution/offset losses.
Calibrate adopted soft-gate thresholds on held-out GestureRef-2 speakers, then audit false rejections by gesture relevance and deictic-word presence.
GestureRef-2 soft-gate calibration card with selected threshold, held-out-speaker rejection rates, and implicit-deixis false-rejection breakdown.
Can soft relevance gating reject same-speaker, trajectory-matched irrelevant gestures without relying on speaker style as referent evidence?
Train ObjectBind with scene-grounded gesture rays and within-speaker counterfactual swaps, using latent-offset contrastive binding to reject style shortcuts.
Compare referent accuracy for ObjectBind, ShiftGuard, and calibration-card-threshold soft gating on GestureRef-2 same-speaker trajectory-matched swaps and ±300-ms offsets.
On unseen-speaker GestureRef-2 trajectory-matched swaps, ObjectBind/ShiftGuard/soft-gate scored 78%/75%/70% aligned and 75%/71%/67% at +300 ms.
Advance ObjectBind to combined stress testing: its 78%/75% aligned/+300-ms swap scores match anchored ShiftGuard’s competing-point scores.
Stress-test ObjectBind on same-speaker, trajectory-matched irrelevant swaps combined with ±300-ms offsets; compare referent accuracy and speaker-probe leakage against anchored ShiftGuard.
Run GestureRef-2 factorial tests combining same-speaker trajectory-matched swaps with ±300-ms offsets; compare ObjectBind and anchored ShiftGuard accuracy and speaker-probe leakage.
GestureRef-2 factorial stress-test report with paired same-speaker swaps, ±300-ms offset accuracy tables, and ObjectBind/anchored ShiftGuard speaker-probe results.
Can ObjectBind distinguish nearby scene objects under imprecise gesture rays without learning speaker-specific pointing biases?
On unseen-speaker GestureRef-2 object pairs separated by ≤10°, ObjectBind gains ≥10 points over speech-only, with binary speaker-probe accuracy ≤55%.
Stratify GestureRef-2 factorial stress-test results by ≤10° object separation; measure ObjectBind’s speech-only accuracy gain and binary speaker-probe accuracy.
On unseen-speaker GestureRef-2 ≤10° object pairs, ObjectBind scored 75% versus speech-only 63%; binary speaker-probe accuracy was 53%.
Retain scene-grounded ObjectBind for close-object trials: it gains 12 points over speech-only with 53% binary speaker-probe accuracy.
Fuse ObjectBind’s scene-grounded rays with anchored ShiftGuard’s deictic assignments through a calibrated offset posterior and within-speaker counterfactual training.
Can the fused offset posterior choose the correct nearby object when deictic timing and gesture rays favor different referents?
Train the fused posterior on GestureRef-2; compare referent accuracy against ObjectBind and anchored ShiftGuard on timing–ray conflicts at ±300 ms.
Benchmark fused posterior, ObjectBind, anchored ShiftGuard, and calibrated soft gate on unseen-speaker GestureRef-2 timing–ray conflicts, irrelevant swaps, and ±300-ms offsets.
On GestureRef-2 timing–ray conflicts, fused accuracy was 79% versus ObjectBind 72% and anchored ShiftGuard 70%; irrelevant-swap/±300-ms losses were 2/3 points.
On newly held-out GestureRef-2 speakers, fusion maintains ≥75% timing–ray-conflict accuracy and ≤5-point irrelevant-swap/±300-ms losses.
Reuse the GestureRef-2 factorial report’s swap/offset protocol; score fusion on new speakers for timing–ray-conflict accuracy and swap/offset losses.
On newly held-out GestureRef-2 speakers, fusion reached 77% timing–ray-conflict accuracy; irrelevant-swap and worst ±300-ms losses were 3/4 points.
Adopt fusion for timing–ray conflicts (77%, ≤4-point robustness losses); retain ObjectBind for ≤10° objects (75% versus speech-only 63%).
Benchmark adopted fusion against ObjectBind, anchored ShiftGuard, and calibration-card-thresholded soft gating on unseen-speaker timing–ray conflicts at ±300 ms.
GestureRef-2 calibration card v2 adds fusion routing criteria and unseen-speaker ±300-ms timing–ray-conflict comparisons to the soft-gate guidance.
Audit calibration card v2 routing on held-out GestureRef-2 speakers, comparing routed accuracy and swap/offset losses against fixed fusion and ObjectBind.
On held-out GestureRef-2, card-v2 routing scored 78% versus fixed fusion 76% and ObjectBind 74%; irrelevant-swap/±300-ms losses were 2/4 points.
Adopt card-v2 routing: 78% held-out accuracy, 2/4-point swap/offset losses, supported by soft gating’s 76% implicit-deixis and ObjectBind’s 75% close-object accuracy.
